title: kubernetes.container.memory.percent is available OOTB with no manual configuration

steps.action: Login as admin; on a fresh install with Kubernetes container monitoring configured, open Metric Explorer for a container object
Search the counter list for kubernetes.container.memory.percent
steps.expected: The KPI is present without any derived counter having been created by hand

title: KPI value equals bytes divided by limit bytes times 100

steps.action: For one container, read kubernetes.container.memory.bytes and kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes for the same collection interval
Read kubernetes.container.memory.percent for that interval and compute (bytes / limit.bytes) * 100
steps.expected: The KPI matches the computed value at the documented precision

title: KPI is derived without any new collection

steps.action: Compare the collection configuration and poll traffic for the container plugin before and after the KPI is enabled
Compare
steps.expected: No additional OID/API call or poll is introduced — the KPI is computed from the two counters already collected

title: Zero memory limit does not raise a division-by-zero or emit a bad value

steps.action: Configure or simulate a container whose kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes is 0 for an interval
Inspect kubernetes.container.memory.percent for that interval
steps.expected: No value is emitted for the interval and no error/exception is logged — the KPI must not record 0, infinity or NaN

title: KPI is not computed when one source counter is missing for the interval

steps.action: Force an interval where memory.bytes is collected but limit.bytes is absent (or vice versa)
Inspect kubernetes.container.memory.percent
steps.expected: No value is emitted for that interval — the KPI computes only when both sources are valid for the same container and the same interval

title: Source counters are unchanged in definition and value

steps.action: Record the definition, unit and a sample of values for kubernetes.container.memory.bytes and kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes before the change
Compare after the KPI ships
steps.expected: Both are byte-identical in definition, collection and values — adding the derived KPI must not alter them

title: limit.bytes is exposed OOTB alongside the new KPI

steps.action: Open the counter list for a Kubernetes container object
Look for kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes
steps.expected: It is now an OOTB counter rather than internal-only, per the agreement recorded on the ticket

title: KPI is selectable in Metric Explorer

steps.action: Open Metric Explorer, pick a container object and select kubernetes.container.memory.percent
Inspect the chart
steps.expected: Values plot as a percentage with a % unit and a sensible 0-100 axis

title: KPI is usable in a dashboard widget

steps.action: Create a dashboard widget on kubernetes.container.memory.percent for a container
View the dashboard
steps.expected: The widget renders the same values as Metric Explorer for the same window

title: KPI is usable in a report

steps.action: Build a report including kubernetes.container.memory.percent and run it
Compare against Metric Explorer for the same window

title: KPI is usable in an alert policy and breaches correctly

steps.action: Create a metric alert policy on kubernetes.container.memory.percent with a threshold of 80% critical, then drive a container above it
Check Active Alerts
steps.expected: A critical alert is raised with the converted percentage in the alert, and clears when utilisation drops below the threshold

title: KPI appears for every container in a multi-container pod

steps.action: Monitor a pod running three containers with different memory limits
Read kubernetes.container.memory.percent per container
steps.expected: Each container has its own value computed from its own limit — values are not shared or aggregated across containers in the pod

title: Container with no memory limit set is handled

steps.action: Monitor a container that declares no memory limit in its spec
Inspect kubernetes.container.memory.percent
steps.expected: The KPI is absent or explicitly not-applicable for that container, and no invalid value is stored

title: Utilisation above 100% is represented faithfully

steps.action: Drive a container to use more than its declared limit if the runtime permits
Inspect kubernetes.container.memory.percent
steps.expected: The value is reported as computed rather than silently clamped to 100, or clamping is documented and consistent between UI, reports and alerts

title: Precision matches the UI and Reports convention

steps.action: Read the same kubernetes.container.memory.percent interval in Metric Explorer, a report and an alert
Compare the decimal places
steps.expected: Identical precision in all three — the ticket requires the conversion precision to match existing UI/Reports behaviour

title: Historical data is not back-filled or corrupted

steps.action: Note the stored history for the two source counters before enabling the KPI
Enable the KPI and re-inspect
steps.expected: Source history is untouched; the KPI has data only from the point it became available, with no fabricated retro values

title: KPI survives an upgrade of an install with existing Kubernetes monitors

steps.action: Upgrade an install already monitoring Kubernetes containers
Check kubernetes.container.memory.percent on a pre-existing container object
steps.expected: The KPI is present and collecting without re-onboarding the cluster

title: RBAC: KPI visibility follows existing counter permissions

steps.action: Log in as a user whose role can view the container object, then as one who cannot
Attempt to read kubernetes.container.memory.percent
steps.expected: Visibility matches the existing per-object permission model — the new KPI introduces no privilege bypass

title: API exposes the KPI under its documented name

steps.action: Query the metric API for kubernetes.container.memory.percent on a container object
Inspect the payload
steps.expected: The counter is named exactly kubernetes.container.memory.percent with a percent unit — no alternative spelling or alias

title: No duplicate or shadow counter is introduced

steps.action: Search the counter list for names containing kubernetes.container.memory
Review the list
steps.expected: Exactly the expected set — bytes, limit.bytes, limit.percent and the new percent. No duplicate, no leftover manually-derived counter shadowing the OOTB one

title: Existing limit.percent counter is unaffected

steps.action: Record values for the pre-existing kubernetes.container.memory.limit.percent counter
Compare after the new KPI ships
steps.expected: Unchanged, and clearly distinguishable from the new percent KPI in every selector so users do not pick the wrong one
